If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test behavior:
  - Valid case: Number[] n = ArrayUtils.addAll(new Number[]{1}, new Long[]{2L}); This should succeed because the destination array type (Number) can hold Long values.
  - Invalid case: n = ArrayUtils.addAll(new Integer[]{1}, new Long[]{2L}); The test expects an IllegalArgumentException, since you cannot store Long into an Integer[].

- Current implementation:
  - In ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2), the method infers the component type from array1:
    - type1 = array1.getClass().getComponentType();
    - It then creates a joined array of type1 and uses System.arraycopy twice:
      - First copies array1 into joinedArray (OK).
      - Then copies array2 into joinedArray (problematic if array2 component type is not assignable to type1).
  - The code around the problematic line:
    - 2961: System.arraycopy(array1, 0, joinedArray, 0, array1.length);
    - 2962: System.arraycopy(array2, 0, joinedArray, array1.length, array2.length);
    - 2963: // Check if problem is incompatible types
    - There is no actual check implemented; only a comment.

- How the bug occurs:
  - For the invalid case (Integer[] with Long[]), the method creates an Integer[] as the destination array (based on array1’s component type).
  - When attempting to copy Long[] into Integer[] at line 2962, System.arraycopy throws ArrayStoreException because Long elements cannot be stored in an Integer[].
  - This matches the bug report’s stack trace: ArrayUtils.addAll(ArrayUtils.java:2962).
  - The test expects a clearer IllegalArgumentException to be thrown by ArrayUtils when array types are incompatible, rather than leaking the low-level ArrayStoreException.

- Root cause:
  - Missing type compatibility handling in ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...). The method does not pre-check whether array2’s component type is assignable to array1’s component type, nor does it catch ArrayStoreException to rethrow an IllegalArgumentException. The inline comment “// Check if problem is incompatible types” indicates the intended but unimplemented check.

- Conclusion:
  - The failure and the bug report are caused by the lack of an explicit incompatibility check or exception translation in ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...). The method should either:
    - Pre-check assignability between array2’s component type and array1’s component type and throw IllegalArgumentException when incompatible, or
    - Catch ArrayStoreException around the second System.arraycopy and rethrow as IllegalArgumentException with a clear message.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
